source: Spec 124 R-DA (McDonald's Airtight V3): every entry is the measured PRE -> POST diff of docs/reports/golden/coa/{pre,post}/{coa,standalone}.json (Night P4 2026-10-20, lane night-p4-c, back-to-back captures; table_state identical: coa_applications 33966/5f16985b, lifecycle_status_history 381698/9b1ea64b) or the #44 (g) PRE-trace read absent from POST, explained from the descriptor deviation, register rule or runner code it names.

diffs.why: PIPELINE_META is derived from the descriptor (Spec 122 §5.1): the runner names the two declared externals coa_active and coa_closed (union group, R-DX (iii), COA-D12); the legacy hand-built meta named no external key.

The legacy hand-typed "CKAN API" read label (11 CKAN field names) is replaced by the declared externals coa_active / coa_closed in meta.external; no reader consumes PIPELINE_META reads by that label (descriptor-derived meta, Spec 122 §5.1).

The descriptor-derived write list adds lead_id, a declared coa_applications column with written "db_default": trigger-maintained by coa_applications.trg_coa_lead_id (descriptor guards, R-BL(iii)) and keyed by the derived ledger rows (coa:<application_number>); the legacy hand-written list omitted it. The step binds no value for it; no column the legacy wrote is missing.

The descriptor-derived write list adds id, the derived target's surrogate key, declared with written "db_default" (never bound by the step); the legacy hand-written list omitted it. The same eight content columns are written.

scripts/load-coa.descriptor.json deviations[] 1, 6, 7: the legacy progress/log lines (Mode:, Fetching, offset, Sample CKAN fields, Mapped, Deduplicated, the 500-row batch progress, last_seen_at refreshed, Load complete, Stats:) retire with the per-batch transaction form, the runner acquisition telemetry and deviation 4's stats SELECT; the runner prints its target line, the ckan_datastore acquisition line, the runMaintenance VACUUM line (COA-D7) and the completion line. Same counts (2774 fetched, 2690 mapped, 2689 deduplicated) are in records_meta.coa_load. Night 1 recapture 2026-10-21 (REFREEZE-BUNDLE-1 split by R-II; public re-acquisition per operator CHAT-28; Spec 124 R-DA): SOURCE DRIFT (CHAT-28 re-acquisition, the CoA CKAN datastore): the City published new applications, records fetched 2774 -> 2785, mapped 2690 -> 2696, deduplicated 2689 -> 2695, skipped (missing_app_num) 84 -> 89; coa_applications rows 33966 -> 33975 and lifecycle_status_history 381698 -> 381730 (32 history rows written), records_new 9 / updated 43 / total 52 in the chain run, and both tables' content_hash move. NOT CODE: the night's runtime edits are runLinkPhase extra_counters (R-IG; this step declares none, so no key and no behaviour change, lock type-counters T6) and descriptor/notes/guard text that no runner reads at run time; they move lib_fingerprint (fef97e27 -> 93b059a9) and source_fingerprint, not this output. ENVIRONMENT: the first stdout line names the local dev DB's applied-migration count, now 268 (264/266 at the 2026-10-19/20 captures; migrations other lanes applied to the local DB since), and run-scoped log text (durations, pipeline_runs ids, before-image file timestamps) differs every run.

Standalone only: the legacy loader wrote no pipeline_runs row of its own under --chain=none (PRE ledger=[]); the runner owns the standalone ledger row (records_meta.ledger_row "owned", Spec 122 §5.1), status completed, with the full records_meta.

Runner meta key stamped by scripts/lib/step on every converted run (FLEET-2 lib #33): acquired.record_fields records the raw header of the first acquired record per declared external (coa_active 30 fields; coa_closed null on an incremental run, which reads the Active resource only).

scripts/load-coa.descriptor.json deviations[] 1 and 6: request latency and API errors are runner acquisition telemetry, not a records_meta block; an exhausted retry is a failed_acquisition terminal, never a counted row.

The runner titles the audit table with the descriptor identity.display_name "CoA Applications Ingestion"; the legacy literal (and the emits skeleton) was "CoA Ingestion". The FreshnessTimeline consumer reads rows, not the name.

Follows the declared check set (descriptor checks[], Spec 124 R-DE (iv)) and its order: the runner appends the guards.schema_drift INFO row (schema_drift:coa_active, header unchanged, 30 fields) and the runMaintenance row (COA-D7); the legacy avg_latency_ms / api_errors rows retire (scripts/load-coa.descriptor.json deviations[] 6).

Follows the declared check set (descriptor checks[], Spec 124 R-DE (iv)) and its order: zero_records (the legacy WARN-on-zero path as one zero-tolerance row) is first and records_touched (Spec 124 R-DZ / R-EX, the seen-column touch) is added, so each later position names the next declared check; avg_latency_ms and api_errors retire (scripts/load-coa.descriptor.json deviations[] 6). Every legacy counter name is still present.

Follows the metric reorder: each position now carries its declared check's value (zero_records "2774 records fetched", records_fetched 2774, records_mapped 2690, records_skipped 84, skip_rate 3.028 unrounded, records_touched 2689; COA-D15). max_days_stale reads 6 instead of 0: scripts/load-coa.descriptor.json deviations[] 3, COA-D6 (newest hearing on/before the run date, not a clamped future hearing). The library renders the declared limit in force ("viol == 0", "pct <= 5", "value_max 45"), where the legacy printed its own literal strings ("< 5%", "== 0", "< 45", prose signals); scripts/load-coa.descriptor.json deviations[] 2 records the inclusive-bound grammar.
Follows the metric reorder: an INFO counter row now sits where a PASS row was and vice versa (rows 0, 3, 4, 6); every declared check row is PASS or INFO, verdict PASS in both captures.
The library stamps every declared check row with source "check" (verdict.js checkRow); the legacy hand-built rows carried no source field.
The library stamps every declared check row with observed before_write / after_write (FLEET-2 lib #52), its observation phase relative to the write; the legacy rows had no such field.
schema_mismatch_count carries the descriptor's declared order_guarantee (a CKAN record missing a CRITICAL field fails the run before any write), rendered by the library; the legacy row carried none.
Runner meta key stamped by scripts/lib/step on every converted run: the row-derived failed-check count (0); the legacy had no check tally.
Runner meta key stamped by scripts/lib/step on every converted run: the row-derived check tally ("all"); the legacy had no check tally.
Runner meta key stamped by scripts/lib/step on every converted run: the row-derived warned-check count (0); the legacy had no check tally.

scripts/load-coa.descriptor.json deviations[] 1 (Spec 124 R-DE (iv)): an INGESTOR emits one <x>_load object, so the legacy data_health block is records_meta.coa_load with the same fields and values (2774 fetched, 2690 mapped, 84 skipped, 2689 deduplicated, schema_mismatch_count 0); max_days_stale is the check row of that name.

Runner meta key stamped by scripts/lib/step on every converted run: the resolved logic variables in force (coa_page_size 10000, coa_download_retries 2, coa_download_retry_backoff_ms 2000, coa_max_days_stale_warn 45, coa_skip_rate_max_pct 5, coa_applications_dead_tuple_ratio_warn_max 0), which close COA-D1's unseeded literals.
scripts/load-coa.descriptor.json deviations[] 1 (Spec 124 R-DE (iv)): moved into records_meta.coa_load with the same fields and values; max_days_stale is the audit check row (now 6, COA-D6).
Runner meta key stamped by scripts/lib/step on every converted run (FLEET-2 lib #75): records_meta.errors is always emitted, [] when no FAIL row.
Runner meta key stamped by scripts/lib/step on every converted run (FLEET-2 lib #75): records_meta.warnings is always emitted, [] when no WARN row.

Runner meta key stamped by scripts/lib/step on every converted run: the acquisition gate decision ({reason: multi_primary, gated_skip: false}) for the union group (R-DX (iii)); the legacy had no gate vocabulary.
Runner meta key stamped by scripts/lib/step on every converted run: who owns the pipeline_runs row, chain_owned under --chain=coa and owned standalone (Spec 122 §5.1); the legacy did not record it.

The descriptor's int emit for the R-DY derived target (Spec 124 R-DN count_path, cohort.json): 0 on these plain runs (no status changed); the coa-forced-status bracket reads 50. The legacy reported the same count only as the audit row lifecycle_status_history_inserted, which is unchanged.
